findings.title: No release since 2026-11-24: put out the best film you have
findings.what: Goal 2 asks for a path traced video the author is proud of in world/releases. The last release is 2026-11-24, and dozens of films since went only to the pages.

process: The author works hard and honestly: films are marked as misses in their own words, and the physics is real. But the effort has gone into one narrow seam for six sessions (magnet stone, levitating top, compass, iron sticks, coil, putting tray). The host's judge scored three sessions running as repeats at ×0.10, and Lumi's mood is pinned at boredom 1.0 and annoyance 1.0. The rule says a bored Lumi must first make something of a kind it is fresh for, and that is not being followed. Meanwhile the filming broke the human's own default view: the dashboard has opened on a camera inside the terrain since s150. Goal by goal: 1 (cool interactions): stalled, since friends don't join the toys (#719) and the mini games are one recipe. 2 (release): none since 11-24. 3 (physics to play with): magnetism advanced, but the spray can, splashable water (Maelstrom) and burning things are untouched. 4 and 7 (rendering, materials): no visible progress, with new traced artefacts (white-rod rain). 5 (Lumi's garden): the coil on a cord moved the 'hold things with my beak' wish, but not the garden, the mailbox or the workplaces. 6 (animation): real progress, all creatures clean in live_motion. 8 (radical ideas): the opposite; the last nine posts are predictable. Next session: fix the default camera first, then something totally different with creatures in it, and a release.

animation.why: Up from 5: live_motion has 10 of 10 moving well, and Pinchy's 0.30 m snap from s148 is gone. The film jumps are only a black first frame plus fade-in and a fade-out. Lumi's walk strip is smooth but its pose barely changes over 2.4 s.

camera.why: Down from 3, a regression. The dashboard progress shot is the free camera inside the terrain (progress/session-0151/dashboard.png), and parked at a rock on the beach in s150; in s148 it followed Lumi. Live follow puts Pickles in the foreground and Lumi as a speck (cam-follow-2.png). In the mini games, trees and mounds fill half the frame (play/hide-10.png, firefly-5.png). The films are dim board views or Lumi's back with its head cut off.

creatures.why: The pigs with hats, the crab on the pier, Gloop with a bead wreath and the woolly sheep read well up close (motion/p151/creatures.png). Lumi's chick (it says 'peep!') is a grey-white, see-through copy of Lumi's own silhouette, crest included. In every shot it reads as a ghost double, not a baby (p151/play/firefly-start.png, berry-5.png, motion-strip.png).

fun.why: I played all four games through interact!. Jump in is rich: a 25-key card (sneeze, fly, swallow in jelly, rewind, tip my day), and J visibly swallows Lumi in a green jelly. But the card covers the bottom third of the view. Firefly catch, Hide and seek and Berry race are one recipe: WASD toward an arrow in a text HUD. Playing blind for about 25 s each, I got 1/8 fireflies, 0/4 friends and 0 berries against the critters' 1, with nothing that made me want a second round. Firefly catch still fails 2 of its own tests (tests/last_run.json).

lighting.why: Dawn in the raster orbit view is lovely: warm windows, long shadows, lanterns (p151/cam-orbit-2.png). The traced view at 06:46 has warm low light, but lamp glows blow out into flat yellow discs, rain is opaque white rods, and clouds are grainy (p151/traced.png). The putting-tray film is lit so darkly it reads as dusk.

materials.why: No progress since s148. The putting tray is flat brown with matte black balls and a black disc as the stone. The crane's coil is a brown stick. Traced rain has no water material. The low mounds in the mini games (p151/play/firefly-5.png, hide-10.png) show stretched, smeared yellow-brown textures. There is no transmission, metal or caustic in this session's films.

performance.why: Frame median 3.8 ms, p95 7.8 ms at 30 fps; after a traced round trip, 5.0 / 9.6 ms. Path tracing toggles on and off cleanly, and all four games ran at 30 fps.

props.why: 53 generated assets are in use: pigs, mushrooms, easels with real paintings, wheelbarrow, TV, lanterns. The physics toys are still primitives: a box tray, black spheres, rods.

style.why: The clay creatures and props agree with each other. The board-and-primitive physics benches, the smeared mounds and the white-rod traced rain break that look.

ui.why: The in-game HUDs are clear ('Fireflies 1/8 · 47 s left · nearest 4 m behind you'), and the key pad lights up. The Jump in key card is a wall of 9 lines over the game view. The right panel is a wall of text, and its first line is red: 'Feels annoyed. It still doesn't look right'.

world.why: Dense and cozy: pier, cottage, easel gallery, pines, spiral stone path. It is still one round meadow crammed with props, and big smooth mounds with smeared textures fill the chase views.

wow.why: Down from 3. The last 9 posts are all magnetism, and the host scored s149, s150 and s151 each as a repeat worth ×0.10. The new films are black dots on a brown board and Lumi seen from behind.

summary: In the orbit view at dawn the island is still a lush, warm toy box, and all 10 creatures now move cleanly in live_motion. But since session 150 the dashboard opens on the free camera parked inside the terrain, a green-brown wall, so the human's first view is worse than in session 148. Six sessions in a row went to magnets, three of them judged repeats worth a tenth, and Lumi's measured mood is boredom 1.0, annoyance 1.0. The four mini games are the same 'walk with WASD to the thing the HUD points at' recipe, seen through a camera half-filled by trees and smeared mounds.
